tagline: First vendor enrolled in the Weather Intelligence Network (WIN) — "South Florida Storm Dispatch." This pressure-washing brand runs a 20-line Smart-DID grid that deliberately overlaps both partner territories: 10 local lines on the Restoration Royalties combo (786·400) and 10 on the FAST Adjusting combo (645·231). When a storm hits, the same lead can move across all three — FAST adjusts the claim, Restoration Royalties restores, Storm Wash cleans — with the app tracking, handing off, and archiving every lead in real time.
demoNote: WIN South Florida Storm Dispatch · dual-territory 20-line pack (786·400 + 645·231) · numbers pending Vitelity selection
insight: a pressure-washing job runs $250–$8,000+ — and the difference between a driveway and a full commercial contract is which line the caller dialed. These calls come in hot: someone is looking at mildew right now, calling three companies off a map, and hiring whoever answers. A phone number that just rings can't sort that. A Smart DID can.

Slots are reserved; real numbers are pulled and assigned before launch — nothing is ever published unowned.
winnetH: South Florida Storm Dispatch — three trades, one network, every lead shared live.
winnetP: Storm Wash is the first vendor enrolled in WIN. It shares the Restoration Royalties territory (786·400) and the FAST Adjusting territory (645·231) on purpose: one storm-driven lead can touch all three trades. The app manages the hand-off, tracking, and archiving — a claim goes to FAST, the restoration goes to Restoration Royalties, and the exterior wash comes here, with every call source-tagged and every lead flowing across the network instead of dying in a voicemail box.
